errors.english: although it produces the preceding mind, it is not apprehended
errors.why: The opponent says the preceding cognition IS a producer (of the later one) yet is not apprehended; the English makes the preceding mind the thing produced.

fix.find: although it produces the preceding mind, it is not apprehended
fix.replace: although the preceding mind is a producer, it is not apprehended

errors.english: The definition of the producer is nothing other than this.
errors.why: The verse says being-apprehended is nothing other than being a producer, i.e. producerhood is the definition of the apprehended (as the prose then states); the English inverts definiens and definiendum.

errors.english: An appearance is never anything other than the apprehended;
errors.why: snang ba here is āloka, light, the stock counter-example of a cause of visual cognition that is allegedly not its object (hence its 'far parts'); rendering it 'appearance' obscures the argument throughout the passage.

errors.english: For the (samskara) mental formation/conditioning to remain stable, it cannot be determined by anything else.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that since the saṃskāra also simply persists, the determination does not come from it; the English turns this into a purpose clause with a different claim.

note: The Pramāṇa argument about the definition of the apprehended object is garbled at several key points; needs real work.
